newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ELWAY MIRACLE PASS SAVES BRONCOS, GIANTS UPSET COWBOYS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ELWAY MIRACLE PASS SAVES BRONCOS, GIANTS UPSET COWBOYS.

text.p: There were miracles aplenty around the NFL Sunday as the Giants upset the Cowboys, Boomer Esiason shot down the Eagles and John Elway kept Denver atop the league with a thrice-deflected touchdown pass.

The Broncos beat the Minnesota Vikings 21-17 when Elway's pass from the 5-yard line with 19 seconds to go was batted twice by defensive back Harlon Barnett in the end zone and knocked back across the goal line by safety Orlando Thomas.
Denver wide receiver Ed McCaffrey snatched the ball out of the air and fell into the end zone for the winning score, capping an 84-yard drive.

"At first I didn't think the ball was going to carry that far, and I was going to make the tackle," said McCaffrey. "Either someone else tipped it again, or the ball carried and I was able to get my hands on it.
"You put it up and hope it comes out this way," said Elway. "This year we have been getting the bounces, things seem to go our way."
"McCaffrey made a great catch," said coach Mike Shanahan. "You have to stay focused. It's not just luck. This was more to add to John Elway's legend."

It was the 34th time Elway has rallied the Broncos, now a league-best 11-1, from a fourth-quarter deficit. Elway, who completed 27-of-36 passes for 334 yards, had his fourth 300-yard game of the season and 32nd of his career.
In East Rutherford, New Jersey, the New York Giants beat the Cowboys 20-6, capitalising on five Dallas turnovers.

Tito Wooten ran back 54 yards for a touchdown in a 13-point second quarter after a Michael Irvin catch and fumble. Cowboys Deion Sanders and fullback Darryl Johnston also had costly fumbles after pass receptions.
"We stunk today and the outcome was evident halfway through," said Dallas coach Barry Switzer.
The Giants gave the game ball to their coach. "I've gotten a lot of game balls, but none more special than this one," said Dan Reeves, expected to be fired after the season
"In the second quarter I knew we were going to win. The defence played great forcing the turnovers."
Dallas has not scored a touchdown in two games.

At Arizona, Esiason's third touchdown pass of the period, a 24-yarder to Marcus Dowdell with 14 seconds left, capped a frenetic fourth quarter and gave the Cardinals a 36-30 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
The teams combined for 37 points in the fourth period, including 24 over the final 2:45.

Esiason was 13-for-16 for 180 yards and three touchdowns in the fourth quarter, finishing 24-for-43 for 367 yards. Considered a candidate for retirement a few weeks ago, he has led the Cardinals to three straight wins since being made a starter.

The Eagles and Cowboys, both 7-5, missed a chance to gain ground in the NFC East because at Washington, Jeff Wilkins' fourth field goal of the game -- a 38-yarder 3:24 into overtime -- lifted the San Francisco 49ers to a 19-16 victory over the Redskins (8-4).
The Niners (9-3) forced the overtime when William Floyd scored on a one-yard run with 1:57 left in the fourth quarter.
At New England, Drew Bledsoe threw for two touchdowns in the first half and Curtis Martin ran for 141 yards as the Patriots bounced the Indianapolis Colts 27-13.
New England (8-4) bounced back from last week's 34-8 loss to Denver and won for the fifth time in six games to stay right behind first-place Buffalo in the AFC East.

In Buffalo, Jim Kelly threw for 176 yards and three scores in the first half before leaving with a hamstring injury and Steve Tasker had a pair of touchdown catches as the Bills routed the New York Jets 35-10.
Buffalo (9-3) beat the league-worst Jets (1-11) for the fourth straight time.
In Chicago, Dave Krieg threw three touchdown passes and Raymont Harris rushed for 122 yards to lead the Bears to a 31-14 victory over the Detroit Lions.

Detroit running back Barry Sanders, who had 21 carries for 107 yards, became the first player to rush for 1,000 yards in eight straight seasons and moved past O.J. Simpson into eighth place on the all-time rushing list.
In Kansas City, Stan Humphries hit Tony Martin with a pair of touchdown passes and Leonard Russell rushed for two scores to lead the San Diego Chargers past the Chiefs 28-14.
San Diego (7-5) swept the season series and moved within a game of the second-place Chiefs (8-4) in the AFC West.
In Baltimore, Mike Hollis kicked a 34-yard field goal with just under six minutes left in overtime to give the Jaguars a 28-25 win over the Ravens.
Jacksonville (5-7) broke a 10-game road losing streak.
In Tampa, Trent Dilfer passed for 253 yards and a touchdown and the Buccaneers beat the New Orleans Saints 13-7 for their third straight win.
In Seattle, Jeff Hostetler threw two touchdown passes and Napoleon Kaufman rushed for 104 yards as the Oakland Raiders snapped a three-game losing streak, 27-21 over the Seahawks.
In Cincinnati, Jeff Blake passed for 349 yards and four touchdowns, including three to Carl Pickens, as the Bengals beat the Atlanta Falcons 41-31.
In Houston, Steve Beuerlein threw three touchdown passes and the Carolina Panthers took advantage of four turnovers for a 31-6 romp past the Oilers.

In St Louis, Brett Favre became just the second quarterback in NFL history to throw for 30 touchdowns in three different seasons as the Green Bay Packers halted a two-game slide by overcoming the Rams 24-9.
Favre completed 25-of-37 passes for 192 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. Miami's Dan Marino has four seasons of 30 or more touchdown passes.
Green Bay (9-3) shares the best record in the NFC with San Francisco.
